source: General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — Sweet Corn Production Handbook (ផលិតកម្មដំណំពោតផ្អែម), in partnership with SNV
text:
Land preparation is an important task for growing corn, ensuring good plant establishment and growth. Equipment and methods can vary depending on the growing region, the season, soil type, and the farmer's own resources. Good practice is to plow and harrow the field thoroughly, plowing 1-2 times at a depth of 15-20 cm.

The purposes of land preparation are: to loosen the soil so it is easy for roots to penetrate and grow well; to remove weeds present in the field; and to destroy pests, diseases, and insects present in the soil.

Corn can be grown in both the dry season and the rainy season, but land preparation methods differ between the two seasons:

Dry season (រដូវប្រាំង): Plowing begins after floodwaters recede and the field has good residual moisture. The soil should be left to dry (sun-exposed/fallow) for a short period, about 5-7 days (this fallow period is meant to let the soil dry out). After 7 days, plow a second time. Land preparation in the dry season should aim to pulverize the soil finely, to help retain soil moisture, since rainfall is very limited in this season and crop growth depends entirely on residual soil moisture.

Rainy season (វស្សា): Plowing in the rainy season differs somewhat from the dry season — plowing begins after the previous dry-season harvest, i.e. in around April. In this season the soil should be left fallow for a longer period, in order to: kill pests, diseases, and reduce certain soil toxins through sun heat; increase soil aeration to help corn roots breathe more easily; kill weeds and aid the breakdown of organic matter in the soil; and loosen the soil to better capture the first rains of the new year/rainy season and to ease the second plowing pass.

General practice: plow and harrow thoroughly, and leave the soil fallow for about 10-15 days with a plowing depth of 10-20 cm to achieve good soil tilth. Apply about 2 kg of organic/natural fertilizer per square meter of bed. Raised beds should be formed 1 meter wide, 20-30 cm high in the rainy season and 30-50 cm high in the dry season, oriented along the length of the field for best results.
